title: Santosha
tagline: Contentment — at peace with what is
description: Contentment — at peace with what is

sutra.meaning: Cleanliness, contentment, discipline, self-study, surrender, these fixed observances refine inner life.

sections.insight: There is always scope for improvement in following all of these Niyamas
sections.reflectionPrompt: Which one needs special attention from me?
sections.practice: Focus on one at a time. Which one is particularly challenging for me.
sections.journalPrompt: What changes was I inspired to make in my life?
sections.gurudevInsight: a) Shaucha b) Santosha c) Tapas d) Swadhaya e) Ishwara Pranidhana are niyamas

sutra.meaning: From contentment, the very best in happiness is obtained.

sections.journalPrompt: What did I have enough of?
sections.gurudevInsight: Happiness again is an attitude. If you are used to being unhappy, even in the best of situation you will still grumble and be unhappy. When you are happy, what is happening? When you are smiling, what is happening? There is so much relaxation in the muscles of your face, in the head, and everywhere. There is freedom, there is joy, and there is relaxation.But if you train your muscles and nervous system to being unhappy, then that same thing continues (unhappiness), that is, the knots in your face, the stiffness in your head, and in your body. You remain unhappy irrespective of the situation around you.

sections.theme: A benevolent mind is a content one.

sutra.meaning: From contentment, and benevolence of consciouness  comes supreme happiness.

sections.practice: Smile through the day notwithstanding the events.
sections.journalPrompt: What all could I smile through today?
sections.gurudevInsight:
Santosha, happiness, contentment gives great joy. The
greatest happiness will come. Just cultivating this attitude of being happy, will in turn not
give you misery, its not just a mood making, it isn’t, but brings you greatest, incomparable
happiness in life.
